title: The Benefits of Fine-Tuning Your Own AI Brain: Using Meta's Muse Glimmer Inside Slack
description: Fine-tune an open-weight agentic model like Meta's Muse Glimmer so your Slack AI agent understands company terminology, workflows, and approvals — then execute actions with tool calling.
excerpt: Adapt the model to your workflows — not the other way around. Fine-tune Muse Glimmer and run a company-specific AI brain inside Slack.

sections.heading: From a general AI to your company's AI brain
sections.content: A general-purpose AI understands CRMs and tickets in the abstract. It does not know that your company calls a workflow Pipeline Rescue, that Slack channels map to customers, or that a specific approval is required before a deal moves. Fine-tuning teaches domain behavior: terminology, request structure, classification, sales handling, tool calling, workflows, and human approval.

sections.heading: Why open-weight models change the equation
sections.content: Closed models limit customization, infrastructure, data control, and cost. Muse Glimmer is a 30-billion-parameter open-weight agentic model that can be downloaded, customized, and deployed — including locally on consumer hardware — with training that combines supervised fine-tuning, on-policy distillation, and reinforcement learning.

sections.heading: Fine-tuning + Slack = an AI operating layer
sections.content: Architecture: Slack → AI Agent → Fine-Tuned Model → Tool Calling → CRM / APIs / Internal Systems → Slack. The model decides. Tools execute. Slack is the interface. Fine-tuning supplies company-specific intelligence.

sections.heading: Why fine-tuning instead of just prompt engineering?
sections.content: A prompt tells the model what to do. Fine-tuning trains it on how your organization actually performs the task. That matters across thousands of repeated interactions. Retrieval, tool calling, structured prompts, and software logic often come first. Fine-tune when the model itself must specialize.

sections.heading: Your AI should understand your business
sections.content: The future of enterprise AI is the model-and-tool combination that understands your business. Combine company knowledge, fine-tuned behavior, tool calling, business APIs, and human approval inside Slack.

faq.question: What is Meta's Muse Glimmer?
faq.answer: Muse Glimmer is a 30-billion-parameter open-weight agentic model from Meta, designed for reasoning, coding, administrative tasks, and other agentic workloads. Unlike closed models accessed only through an API, it can be downloaded, customized, and deployed to your infrastructure.

faq.question: Why fine-tune an open-weight model instead of using a closed AI API?
faq.answer: Closed models are powerful but limit customization, infrastructure, data control, and cost. Open-weight models let you download, fine-tune, and deploy according to your requirements — so you adapt the model to your workflows instead of adapting workflows to a generic assistant.

faq.question: When should you fine-tune instead of using prompt engineering?
faq.answer: Prompt engineering tells a model what to do in a prompt. Fine-tuning trains it on examples of how your organization actually performs the task. That matters when the same behavior must happen consistently across thousands of interactions.

faq.question: How does a fine-tuned model work inside Slack?
faq.answer: The architecture is Slack → AI Agent → Fine-Tuned Model → Tool Calling → CRM / APIs / Internal Systems → Slack. The model handles understanding and decision-making. Tool calling gives access to real business capabilities. Slack is the interface.

faq.question: Should every company fine-tune a model for Slack?
faq.answer: No. Retrieval, tool calling, structured prompts, and traditional software logic often solve parts of the problem more efficiently. Fine-tune when the model itself needs to become specialized.
